findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). 

It was observed that the dish machine is not reaching a heat sanitizing temperature of above 150F. A follow up is scheduled for 2/10/2025 to ensure that the dish machine is reaching a temperature of above 160F. Ensure that dish machines are properly sanitizing dishes by reaching a temperature of 160F or above.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
The facility has evidence of rodent activity in the canteen. Droppings are observed on the floor, in the base cabinet under the sink, and on the back ledge of the counter behind the sink. There also appears to be droppings under the popcorn maker at the far back corner. A follow up inspection will be conducted on 12/01/23 to ensure that there is no evidence of rodent activity. Traps have been empty and bait stations outside have had minimal activity. A increased measures will be added to the canteen area to ensure that rodents have been eliminated from the facility. The facility has regular pest control. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Evidence of rodent activity is present at the canteen area on the counter, in the base cabinet under the sink and on the floor. More regular cleaning is required to remove evidence of rodent activity and maintain the area clean.  

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.115: (A) Live animals may not be allowed on PREMISES of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT (B) Live animals may be allowed on PREMISE under certain conditions if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES does not occur. (C) Live or dead FISH bait may be stored if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES is prevented. 

Inspector observed signs of pest activity under the cold holding line and in the concession area by the doors of the cafeteria. The facility has contracted a pest control company that is actively working to eradicate any pests in the building along with sealing and catching on the outside of the building before pests have a chance to enter.  PCO was present for the inspection and said that they are present on site every other day to verify and replace control methods as needed. A spot check will be conducted by email on the 17th to verify PCO operation via log sheets. If there is continued improvement observed during the evaluation of records, an in person spot check will be conducted on November 6th after the new garage door has been installed. New door sweeps have also been orderd and will be in this week. Maintenance will place new door sweeps.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Some evidence of pest activity is observed under the cold holding area and in the concession area by the doors to the cafeteria. Continue to monitor, clean and sanitize the areas daily.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds. 

Inspector observed the dish machine to require 7 run cycles before it began to register proper sanitizing temperature on a digital maximum registering thermometer. The inspector observed that the pressure was low initially. Also the wash water temperature gage never did come up to 150F. The gage may be broken or the water may not be hot enough. The facility is calling for the machine to be maintenanced. Until that time, wash and rinse can be completed in the machine but sanitize  should be done in the three part sinks with 200ppm of chlorine per the label directions. Air dry the food contact items.  

The item is considered corrected on site as the machine will not be used for sanitizing. Sanitizing will be conducted via the three part sink. The items will then be air dried. A spot check will be conducted on the machine during the 10/2/23 follow up for a different violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Chlorine in the three part sink was set up for use at 10 ppm of chlorine. The employee who made the solution was trained on site, Ensure that the employees doing the task are properly trained on that task. Follow label directions for sanitizing. The violation is considered corrected on site as coaching was provided.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Inspector observed evidence of mice in the cabinets and on the floor of the concession area of the cafeteria, in the soda machine cabinet, under the cold holding service line, in the back by the desk and in curbed area. Clean and sanitize these areas thoroughly and carefully so that historical evidence of rodents can be eliminated and any continued activity can be monitored.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Inspector observed single use utensils presented for service in plastic containers that allow the mixing of the handles and food contact ends of the utensils. Provide a dispenser that does not allow for contamination of the food contact ends of the single service utensils.
